sentences: Learning parity with noise observes random linear equations whose labels are only slightly more likely to be correct than incorrect.
The source studies learners restricted to a small working memory while processing a stream of these equations.
It conjectures that avoiding exponentially many samples requires memory of order n squared divided by epsilon squared, where epsilon is the bias toward correct labels.
The proved lower bound has a weaker dependence on that bias.
Matching it would quantify how little per-sample information forces a learner to retain increasingly large state, beyond noiseless parity-learning barriers.
